newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, October 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, October 15.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* The government is discussing the removal of the heads of secret services (all).
* Pds leader Massimo D'Alema says Justice minister Giovanni Maria Flick was right to reprove magistrates in La Spezia and Milan: "There is no conflict between politics and magistrates" (all).
* Public works minister and ex magistrate Antonio Di Pietro defends his former colleagues in Milan and says they should go ahead (all).

* Ruling coalition parties are split over the "war of drugs" after chemists decided to protest against the 1997 budget by charging consumers the full price of drugs which are normally paid by the national health system. People will have to ask for refunds directly from public health service (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi says he wants the lira to return to the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (Erm) by the end of the year. Ciampi also says he supports "every measure which would strenghten the 1997 budget, in quality as in quantity" (all).
* Ciampi signed a decree enabling the Treasury to sell its 60 percent ordinary share capital stake in ailing Banco di Napoli (all).

* Financial Holding group Gemina says it intends to launch its new holding group, called Holding Partecipazioni Industriali (HPI), on November 27. HPI will include publishing group Rizzoli, sports clothing Fila, paper group Burgo and other divisions (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
